properties.headline: Tornado Warning issued October 4 at 4:20PM CDT until October 4 at 4:30PM CDT by NWS Mobile AL
properties.description:
At 420 PM CDT, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing a tornado
was located 5 miles east of Fort Morgan, or 10 miles east of Dauphin
Island, moving northeast at 5 mph.

HAZARD...Tornado.

SOURCE...Radar indicated rotation.

IMPACT...Flying debris will be dangerous to those caught without
shelter. Mobile homes will be damaged or destroyed. Damage
to roofs, windows, and vehicles will occur.  Tree damage is
likely.

This tornadic thunderstorm will remain over mainly rural areas of
south central Baldwin County.
properties.instruction:
TAKE COVER NOW! Move to a basement or an interior room on the lowest
floor of a sturdy building. Avoid windows. If you are outdoors, in a
mobile home, or in a vehicle, move to the closest substantial shelter
and protect yourself from flying debris.

Torrential rainfall is occurring with this storm, and may lead to
flash flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flooded roadways.

properties.description:

due to elevated surf of 3 to 6 feet. Abnormally high morning
and evening tides of 6.5 to 7 ft is expected.

* WHERE...Catalina and Santa Barbara Islands, Ventura County
Beaches, Malibu Coast and Los Angeles County Beaches. Most
susceptible areas will be Long Beach and Avalon Harbor Tuesday
and Wednesday. Then, Mailbu to Ventura Wednesday through
Friday.

* WHEN...From Tuesday afternoon through Friday evening.

* IMPACTS...There is an increased risk of ocean drowning. Rip
currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Waves can
wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats
nearshore. Moderate flooding of sea water is possibly over
some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the
morning and evening high tides, including over beach parking
lots, bike paths, and harbor walkways. Moderate beach erosion
is possible to likely.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...There is a moderate chance that an
upgrade to Coastal Flood Advisory and/or High Surf Advisory
will be needed. These products will likely need to be extended
into the weekend.
properties.instruction:
Remain out of the water due to hazardous swimming conditions, or
stay near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly
in such conditions, stay off the rocks.

properties.areaDesc: Death Valley National Park
properties.headline: Extreme Heat Warning issued October 4 at 12:33PM PDT until October 9 at 8:00PM PDT by NWS Las Vegas NV
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously hot conditions with high temperatures near 110
degrees and overnight lows only getting down to around 85 degrees.
This will yield at least major heat risk, impacting anyone without
adequate cooling and hydration.

* WHERE...Elevations in Death Valley National Park below 2000 feet.

* WHEN...Until 8 PM PDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Heat related illnesses increase significantly during
extreme heat events.
properties.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

Do not leave young children and pets in unattended vehicles. Car
interiors will reach lethal temperatures in a matter of minutes.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose
fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early morning
or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and
heat stroke.

To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and
Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

Monitor the latest forecasts and warnings for updates.

properties.areaDesc: Yuma
properties.headline: Extreme Heat Watch issued October 4 at 11:38AM MST until October 8 at 8:00PM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously hot conditions possible. Afternoon temperatures
104 to 107. Major Heat Risk.

* WHERE...Yuma.

* WHEN...From Wednesday morning through Thursday evening.

* IMPACTS...Heat related illnesses increase significantly during
extreme heat events. Overexposure can cause heat cramps and heat
exhaustion to develop and, without intervention, can lead to heat
stroke.
properties.instruction:
An Extreme Heat Watch means that a period of very hot temperatures,
even by local standards, may occur. Actions should be taken to lessen
the impact of the extreme heat.

Take extra precautions if you work or spend time outside. When
possible, reschedule strenuous activities to early morning or
evening. Know the signs and symptoms of heat exhaustion and heat
stroke. Wear lightweight and loose-fitting clothing when possible and
drink plenty of water.

To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and
Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

Public cooling shelters are available in some areas. Consult county
officials for more details.

properties.areaDesc: City and Borough of Juneau
properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 4 at 10:24AM AKDT until October 4 at 1:45PM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
properties.description:
Heavy rain overnight into this morning has led to a rise in Montana
Creek. The creek is expected to crest this morning then fall back
below minor flood by this afternoon as rain rates lower.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Montana Creek near areas near the low water crossing on
Montana Creek Road and near Back Loop Road at the Montana Creek
bridge.

* WHEN...Until 145 PM AKDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Water over roadways.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1024 AM AKDT, river gauge reports indicate rises in water
levels from heavy rain across the advisory area. Minor flooding
is ongoing or expected to begin shortly, especially near Montana
Creek. Between 1.25 and 1.75 inches of rain have fallen.
Additional rainfall amounts of 0.25 to 0.5 inches are possible.
- For Montana Creek at Back Loop Bridge:
At 10:00am the stage was 14.9 feet.
Flood Stage is 14.5 feet.
Forecast: A crest around 15.0 feet is expected around 11:00am
Sunday.

Impacts:
At 14.5 feet: Water begins flowing over the low water crossing on
Montana Creek Road. Bankfull conditions at the gauge with water
starting to inundate adjacent undeveloped fields along Mendenhall
Loop Road.
At 15.5 feet: Up to one half foot of water will flow over the low
water crossing on Montana Creek Road after the community gardens.
Water will approach and begin to inundate yards of residences along
the Northwest side of Mendenhall Loop Road.
properties.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

properties.areaDesc: Guam; Rota; Tinian; Saipan
properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued October 5 at 3:56AM ChST until October 5 at 4:00PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 7 to
10 feet in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk,
dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...North, west, and south facing reefs of Guam, Rota, Tinian
and Saipan.

* WHEN...Until 4 PM ChST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Elevated swells coming from the southwesterly
monsoon surge and Typhoon Choi-wan (26W) to the north will allow
advisory-level surf and a high risk of rip currents to continue.
properties.instruction:
Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions. Rip currents will be life threatening. If
caught in a rip current, relax and float. Don't swim against the
current. If able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If
unable to escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 4 at 11:29AM CDT until October 5 at 8:00AM CDT by NWS Mobile AL
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents.
For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding
expected.

* WHERE...In Alabama, Mobile Coastal and Baldwin Coastal
Counties. In Florida, Escambia Coastal, Santa Rosa Coastal and
Okaloosa Coastal Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Rip Current Risk, through Monday evening.
For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from midnight tonight to 8 AM
CDT Monday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only
isolated road closures expected. Rip currents can sweep even
the best swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 4 at 8:11AM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
A system moving through the area is bringing with it periods of
snow and rain to Isabel Pass. Warming weather during the morning
will see snow change over to rain during daytime hours. Cooling
conditions overnight will lead to refreezing of previous snow-melt
and rain on roadways, creating particularly slick and slippery
conditions.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 4 at 11:10AM CDT until October 5 at 12:00AM CDT by NWS Mobile AL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of southwest Alabama, including the following
areas, Baldwin Central, Baldwin Coastal, Baldwin Inland, Mobile
Central, Mobile Coastal and Mobile Inland and northwest Florida,
including the following areas, Escambia Coastal, Escambia Inland,
Okaloosa Coastal, Okaloosa Inland, Santa Rosa Coastal and Santa
Rosa Inland.

* WHEN...Through this evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas. Storm drains
and ditches may become clogged with debris.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Multiple rounds of heavy rainfall are expected through this
afternoon. Additional rainfall amounts of 2 to 4 inches are
expected with locally higher amounts of up to 6 inches possible.
This may lead to flash flooding, especially in urban and poor
drainage areas.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

properties.areaDesc: Interstate 5 Corridor; Santa Clarita Valley; Santa Susana Mountains; Western San Gabriel Mountains and Highway 14 Corridor
properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued October 3 at 8:35PM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...The South Coast AQMD has issued an air quality alert due to
increased fine particle pollution from wildfire smoke.
Visit https://www.aqmd.gov/alertinfo to check current and forecasted
air quality levels.

* WHERE...in the Santa Clarita Valley, the I-5 corridor, and the
Angeles National Forest. Levels of particle pollution can vary by
time and location depending on fire activity and local weather
conditions.

* WHEN...8 PM Saturday until 8 PM Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Particles in wildfire smoke can get deep into the lungs
and cause serious health problems such as heart attacks, strokes,
asthma attacks, and difficulty breathing. Everyone can be affected,
but people with lung or heart disease, older adults, people who are
pregnant, children, and those who spend a lot of time outdoors are
at greater risk.
properties.instruction:
To protect your health, if you smell or see smoke:

* Remain indoors with windows and doors closed
* Avoid intense outdoor physical activity
* Run your air conditioner and/or an air purifier
* If you must be outdoors, keep the time brief and wear a well-
fitting N-95 mask
* Do not use whole house fans or swamp coolers that bring in
outside air if you have other methods to stay cool
* Avoid other sources of pollution such as fireplaces, candles,
incense, grilling, and gasoline-powered lawn and garden
equipment
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

NWSheadline: AIR QUALITY ALERT FOR HARMFUL FINE PARTICLE POLLUTION LEVELS DUE TO WILDFIRE SMOKE

properties.areaDesc: Coastal North Bay Including Point Reyes National Seashore; San Francisco Peninsula Coast; Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast
properties.headline: Heat Advisory issued October 3 at 7:48PM PDT until October 4 at 10:00PM PDT by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Hot conditions with maximum temperatures in the low-80s to
low-90s. Mild minimum temperatures and weak onshore flow will limit
overnight relief.

* WHERE...Southern Monterey Bay and the Big Sur Coast, Coastal North
Bay Including Point Reyes National Seashore, and San Francisco
Peninsula Coast.

* WHEN...Until 10 PM PDT Sunday.

* IMPACTS...This level of heat affects anyone without effective
cooling and/or adequate hydration. Impacts likely in some health
systems, heat-sensitive industries and infrastructure.
properties.instruction:
Hydration is a critical piece to surviving the heat. Drink water, and
if possible, take water to those who are vulnerable.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose
fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to the early
